faq.q: Why do plant cells have a cell wall?
faq.a: The cell wall is made of cellulose, a strong fibre. It gives the cell a fixed shape and stops it bursting when it fills with water.
asks: Tell me about the cell wall
What is the cell wall made of?

faq.a: The vacuole is a large bag of cell sap. When it is full of water it presses against the cell wall and keeps the plant firm. When a plant is short of water, the vacuoles shrink and the plant wilts.
Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, which absorbs light. They use that energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water in photosynthesis.

faq.q: Do all plant cells have chloroplasts?
faq.a: No. Cells in roots and in the middle of stems get no light, so they usually have no chloroplasts. Leaf cells have the most.

faq.q: Do plant cells have mitochondria too?
faq.a: Yes. Plants respire all day and night, just like animals, so their cells have mitochondria to release energy from glucose.

facts: Plant cell walls are made mainly of cellulose, the most common natural polymer on Earth.
Plant cells contain mitochondria as well as chloroplasts.
Root cells usually have no chloroplasts because they receive no light.

quiz.say: Which part is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
quiz.show: Which part is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
quiz.why: Only plant cells (and some others, like fungi and bacteria) have a cell wall; animal cells do not.

wrong.0: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus.
wrong.2: Both kinds of cell have a cell membrane.

quiz.say: A plant wilts on a hot day. Which part of its cells has lost water?
quiz.show: A plant wilts on a hot day. Which part of its cells has lost water?
quiz.why: The vacuole holds most of the cell's water. When it shrinks, it stops pressing on the wall and the plant droops.

wrong.0: Chloroplasts make food; they are not the main water store.
wrong.1: The wall stays stiff; it is the vacuole inside that loses water.
